:::{#thm-outer-product-transpose}
#### The transpose of an outer product

For a vector $\vecf{u}$ of length $m$
and a vector $\vecf{v}$ of length $n$,
the [transpose](linear-algebra.qmd#def-matrix-transpose)
of the [outer product](#def-outer-product) $\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}$
is the outer product $\oprod{\vecf{v}}{\vecf{u}}$:

$$
\underbrace{\tp{\paren{\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}}}}_{n \times m}
= \underbrace{\oprod{\vecf{v}}{\vecf{u}}}_{n \times m}
$$

:::

::: proof

Entry $(i, j)$ of each side, for $i$ from $1$ to $n$ and $j$ from $1$ to $m$:

$$
\ba
\sb{\tp{\paren{\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}}}}_{ij}
&= \paren{\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}}_{ji}
&& \text{(definition of the transpose)}
\\
&= u_j v_i
&& \text{(entries of an outer product)}
\\
&= v_i u_j
&& \text{(multiplication of numbers is commutative)}
\\
&= \paren{\oprod{\vecf{v}}{\vecf{u}}}_{ij}
&& \text{(entries of an outer product)}
\ea
$$

:::
